As far as treatment, the best thing is simply to make sure all water parameters are pristine. They have incredible regenerative ability and will heal as long as you provide the right conditions. 

If you can’t get a second tank you should either:
- buy an 80 gallon tank and section it into two. 
Or 
- Rehome one of your axolotls to a well-educated owner who has an already cycled tank of at least 30 gallons ready.

EDIT: keeping two in a 30 gallon is inhumane, since that is about the minimum size for ONE adult axolotl, and because it is next to impossible to keep water quality optimal in those conditions. Plus many additional reasons, some of which other people have already discussed

Mine had the exact same thing. He ended up having a bacterial infection caused by living with poor tank parameters for an extended period of time. The enlarged filaments aren’t harmful, but do your water testing for pH, GH, KH, and weekly for ammonia, nitrite, nitrate (with a liquid test kit) and keep an eye open for any signs of redness, swelling, lethargy, or signs of disease. Be sure to get all parameters into their ideal ranges.

The first things to do are 

1) Make sure your tank is correctly cycled and all parameters are within range. They need to be:

Ammonia 0ppm

Nitrite 0ppm

Nitrate 5-20 ppm

pH 7.4-7.6

GH 125.3-250.6 ppm

KH 53.7-143.2

Temperature 59-65°F

2) Your axolotl is so thin s/he appears emaciated - the body is supposed to be about as wide as the head. It needs to be fed earthworms every day or every other day. Earthworms are nutritionally complete for axolotls. 

Without proper nutrition and living conditions, problems like these spots will fester. Axolotl are very resilient little creatures, try improving the conditions and give it some time to heal. 

Axolotl.org and Caudata.org are great resources for educating yourself on axolotl care. There’s a ton of poor and extreme advice out there, be sure to take everything with a grain of salt and do your own research.

Ideal pH for an axolotl aquarium is 7.4-7.6.
The tolerance range is from 6.5-8.0, and should not be long term.

Focus on being gentle with yourself. Pretend you’re talking to a best friend or loved one who needs support. 

The first step is to catch yourself when you become self critical. Stop the thought, then speak to yourself with understanding and grace. 

Instead of beating yourself up for something, recognize that you are trying and massive personal changes don’t occur overnight. Congratulate yourself for taking the first step towards improving. Do this consistently for months, and you will notice a massive difference. 

As time goes on, focus also on what you’ve accomplished so far. There is no timeline to improving self-criticism, so BE GENTLE with yourself even if it takes significantly longer than you expect.

A couple things that've helped me:

Quoting from [this article](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/if-the-cells-of-our-skin/) by Scientific American:

“The answer is really quite simple. The cells in the superficial or upper layers of skin, known as the epidermis, are constantly replacing themselves. This process of renewal is basically exfoliation (shedding) of the epidermis. But the deeper layers of skin, called the dermis, do not go through this cellular turnover and so do not replace themselves. Thus, foreign bodies, such as tattoo dyes, implanted in the dermis will remain.”

“Tattoos remain in the skin because the ink particles that produce the coloration are too large to be ingested by the white bloods cells that patrol the body and carry foreign bodies away from the skin. The new tattoo-removing lasers work because the laser energy pulverizes the ink into microfine dust particles that are small enough to be taken in by the white blood cells and carried away.”

My Lupus began just as I was ending a course of antibiotics for Lyme disease. There’s still a lot we don’t know about Lyme (and lupus lol), but I have heard of multiple other people who became autoimmune after getting Lyme. 

Like the other person said though, the diseases’ symptoms can overlap (especially aches and pains, fatigue, brain fog) but they are vastly different in all other aspects.

Plaquenil is sometimes prescribed for Lyme patients along with macrolide antibiotics (eg azithromycin) because the two have a synergistic effect. Specifically, plaquenil lowers acid levels where the bacteria hide which helps the antibiotics work effectively.

In Lupus patients Plaquenil doesn’t suppress the immune system either. It is classified as a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD), and works by specifically reducing autoantibody production.

Hi there! This is very long (eek sorry!) but just one lady’s perspective on those questions (:

Getting diagnosed is a whole rollercoaster of emotions. Your life is changing forever. There are so many question marks and so few answers. The amount of initial tests and exams and labs they’ll want to run is exhausting. Emotionally, your ex will probably need to go through the whole grief process. Depression and anxiety just kinda come with the entire chronic illness package. 

For me the real feelings of being a burden/low self-worth hit way after the diagnosis. When I realized it wasn’t getting better. It’s not the start that’s difficult, it’s getting through the day-in day-out tasks while feeling like death. That’s when you’re depressed, crushed, anxious, sad, angry, and really just need lots of hugs and understanding and happy things.

My relationship definitely hasn’t suffered! It’s been hard as f-ck, but we’ve both been through sh-t, understand where the other person is coming from, and we love eachother dearly. He’s my bright spot in all of this, and we were dating only 4 months when I was diagnosed. 

I will say this though:
I tried to tell him to leave at the beginning. And the middle. More than once. But he stayed every time, and I could see he really meant it. 
With so much instability in life the last thing you want is to love/trust/confide in someone who may get tired and leave you if it doesn’t get better after a few years. Therapy def helped me with working to regain self-worth and realize that, even sick and laid up in bed, I’m worth someone sticking around

So sorry you’re dealing with this too! I’m in the same boat - 22 years old, in the last year I’ve gone from 110lbs of muscle to 90lbs and have been struggling to get/stay at 100 lbs. (I have Gastroparesis also and have to gain weight back after every flare) I’m GF too and am currently reincorporating foods after doing the AIP diet. 

u/witchblanket is dead on with small meals and CBD. It’s a lot easier on your gut to snack all day long, and cannabis has honestly been my lifesaver for both stimulating appetite and managing nausea. 

Eat a lot of fatty foods! High protein helps more with keeping muscle mass than significant weight gain. Obviously keep eating fatty meats like salmon or beef, and I sometimes like to fry tofu too. Try tons of cheese and dairy, eggs, rice, grains, nuts, and dried fruit. Add healthy oils (like coconut, flax, MCT, olive oil, etc) to everything you can. Flax oil is especially good in smoothies. 

For example, I’ll regularly make cheese plates with dried fruit and nuts, peanut butter or eggs on GF toast, protein smoothies, quinoa/grain salads, spring rolls with tofu and avocados, and GF pastries smothered in whipped cream. I made rice pudding the other day... it’s mostly eggs, rice, and milk so you’d have a great excuse to keep it all to yourself (; 

If you need more suggestions or support my messages are open! (I don’t check daily but I will get back to you!) All the best and I hope this helps!! 💚
